title: Route scalar callers through existing SIMD dispatch
description:
Quick wins where the SIMD kernel already exists in `gf2-kernels-simd` but the scalar caller never dispatches through it. Each task in this story is a V0→V3 jump in one hop — wire + bench + asm verify.

## Background

`gf2-core` has three places where existing AVX2 dispatch is bypassed: `BitMatrix::matvec` computes parity with scalar `count_ones() % 2` while `popcnt_fn` exists; `BitMatrix::mul` non-M4RM path uses scalar inner-product while `xor_fn` exists; and `gfp::FieldVec` falls back to scalar element-wise loops for any prime not in `{65537, 2^31-1}` despite the `SimdVecOps` infrastructure being in place.

This story has three child tasks (one per call-site). Each follows the per-kernel execution protocol from the epic spec doc: pinned baseline → asm artefact → perf-stat → proptest equivalence → $\geq 1.5\times$ geomean → single-step commit → lead-only gate transitions.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] Each child task ships per the per-kernel execution protocol (baseline saved, asm inspected, perf-stat captured, proptest equivalence, $\geq 1.5\times$ geomean at design size class).
- [hard] No `unsafe` introduced outside `gf2-kernels-simd`.
- [hard] No regression on existing benches at sizes below each kernel's crossover threshold.

## Notes

Highest-ROI tasks in the epic — the SIMD already exists, only routing is missing. Spec doc: `dev/plans/gf2_core_ppc_spiral.md`.
